composio.note: Composio provides a managed Gmail OAuth app, which is the default. Users see 'Composio wants to access your account' and quota is shared across Composio users.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes: Composio's managed Gmail app works. For production you likely need your own app so users see your brand, get dedicated quota, and can use scopes the managed defaults lack.

prerequisites.title: Google Cloud project and consent screen
prerequisites.detail: Configure the OAuth consent screen (branding, audience, scopes) in the Google Auth platform. It cannot be removed once configured.

prerequisites.title: Public home page and privacy policy
prerequisites.detail: The home page must be publicly accessible, and the privacy policy must be on the same domain and disclose how Google user data is used.

prerequisites.title: Verified domain ownership
prerequisites.detail: Verify ownership of the project's authorized domains in Google Search Console.

prerequisites.title: Budget and a Google-approved assessor
prerequisites.detail: Restricted scopes on servers need an annual assessment by a third party. One vendor report cites $15,000-$75,000.

steps.title: Choose the narrowest scopes
steps.detail: Map each agent feature to the least-privileged Gmail scope and flag which are non-sensitive, sensitive or restricted.
steps.done_when: Scope list with classification and justification drafted

steps.title: Create project and configure consent screen
steps.detail: Set app name, support email, audience (Internal or External) and contact email, and accept the API Services User Data Policy.

steps.title: Create OAuth client and Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the OAuth client, copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard, then create the Gmail auth config with your client ID and secret via Composio's API.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists and a test connection works

steps.title: Prepare home page, privacy policy, domain
steps.detail: Publish a public home page and a privacy policy on the same domain, and verify the domain in Search Console.

steps.title: Draft justifications and demo script
steps.detail: Write per-scope justifications explaining why narrower scopes are not enough, and a script for an English demo video. Keep the consent-screen scopes identical to the submission.

steps.title: Record and upload demo video
steps.detail: Show the full OAuth grant in English, the consent screen with the app name, and each scope's functionality. Upload to YouTube as Unlisted.

steps.title: Verify and publish branding
steps.detail: Click Verify Branding, then Publish branding within 7 days of a compliant result.

steps.title: Submit scope verification
steps.detail: Submit in the OAuth Verification Center. Delete unused OAuth clients first.

steps.title: Wait for Google review
steps.detail: Check the Verification Center and email; Trust & Safety may ask for more information.

steps.title: Complete security assessment
steps.detail: Hire a Google-approved assessor and complete the assessment for restricted scopes on servers.

steps.title: Get org admin approval if needed
steps.detail: Ask your organization's admin to approve or allowlist the app.

traps.title: Restricted scopes cost time and money
traps.detail: Most agent features (read, modify, compose) use restricted scopes, so a server-side app needs an annual third-party assessment.

traps.title: Scope mismatches cause rejections
traps.detail: A developer was rejected when consent-screen scopes differed from the submission, and the 1,000-character justification limit made multi-scope explanations hard.

traps.title: Unverified apps hit a 100-user cap
traps.detail: Unverified apps requesting sensitive or restricted scopes show warnings and are capped at 100 total users.

traps.title: Testing status expires access
traps.detail: Apps in Testing have a test-user list, a tester warning and limited refresh token lifetime, so they are not suitable for production.

traps.title: Brand verification expires in 7 days
traps.detail: If you do not publish branding within 7 days of a compliant result, you must re-run it.

traps.title: Branding is frozen during review
traps.detail: Branding changes are not allowed while verification is in progress.

traps.title: Review emails may not arrive
traps.detail: One developer reported many rejections with no emails, so check the Verification Center manually.

traps.title: Callback domain cannot be verified by you
traps.detail: Google requires verified domains, but Composio's callback domain is not yours to verify. Route the callback through your own domain with a redirect proxy that returns a 302.

blockers.what_it_means: The app exceeded its new-user authorization rate limit or total new user cap.
blockers.what_to_do: Check the grant rate on the consent screen page, finish verification, or request a quota increase (Google says to expect a response in 5 business days).

blockers.what_it_means: The app has not completed verification.
blockers.what_to_do: Submit a verification request, or use a Workspace admin Trusted label for internal users.

blockers.symptom: Review asks for test login credentials
blockers.what_it_means: Reviewers need a working login to see the app, which one developer reported for an internal-use app.
blockers.what_to_do: Create a test account and include credentials in the submission.
